title: Check two changed-contact P104 braids and a partial port
body:
Cross-chain reuse of an arm fails an exact formal seam monomial condition. An explicit 578-event hub bypass passes both formal operator orientations with six QUERYs and complete BIT margin about −212.8398141868 at the first trial. The projected 679-row interface and 37-root caller also pass formally. They still require four seam QUERYs, losing 7.8433904319 with granted discard and 9.8433904319 with the two-QUERY formal clean restore.

## Task and overlap

This refines the #7952 `755fcee748d4e90feda281f27d06e7bc66ecf954` caller by changing actual contacts. The fixed two-IDLE model #7964 `1f90b620855e08b6a941a304ed25eda5600c0deb` studies a different family. All 36 original native obligations and the 48-call rational comparator are priced. The scoped task is the #7852 follow-up at `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`, based on `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` and #7830 `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive gives exact source identities and complete assumptions.

## Validation

Extract and verify `SHA256SUMS`, then run the README commands with Python 3.12 and assertions enabled. The independent cold replay reproduced both literal changed callers and three receipts byte-for-byte, checked full formal forward and adjoint actions, and replayed the pinned rational and baseline caller receipts.

## Open next questions

Couple a different port restriction with a better native tariff or altered reader schedule. Changed native charts, physical basis and disposal/erasure, precision and complete outer application remain open.
